absement.desc: Absement measures the accumulated distance covered by an object over time, taking into account both speed and direction of motion.

absorbed-dose-rate.desc: Absorbed dose rate is the amount of energy deposited in a given material per unit of mass over a specific time period.

acceleration.desc: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time.

amount-of-substance.desc: Amount of substance is a measure of the number of entities (atoms, molecules, ions) in a sample, expressed in moles.

angular-acceleration.desc: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity over time, measured in radians per second squared.

angular-momentum.desc: Angular momentum is a measure of rotational motion, action is a physical quantity related to energy, and spin is an intrinsic property of particles.

angular-velocity.desc: Angular velocity refers to the rate of change of angular displacement of an object. Radioactive activity is the rate of decay of radioactive material.

area.desc: Area is a measure of the amount of space enclosed by a two-dimensional shape, such as a square or circle. It is expressed in square units.

area-density.desc: Area density is the measure of mass per unit area of a surface, expressed in units like kg/m^2 or g/cm^2.

capacitance.desc: Capacitance is the ability of a system to store electric charge, measured in farads. It determines the amount of charge a capacitor can hold.

catalytic-activity-concentration.desc: Catalytic activity concentration refers to the amount of catalyst present in a reaction, influencing the reaction rate.

centrifugal-force.desc: Centrifugal force is a fictitious force that acts outward on an object moving in a curved path, caused by inertia.

chemical-potential.desc: Chemical potential is the energy required to add one mole of a substance to a system at constant temperature and pressure.

crackle.desc: Crackle is a measure of the sound produced when something is crushed or broken, often indicating the presence of moisture or impurities.

currency.desc: Currency is a medium of exchange for goods and services, typically in the form of paper or coins issued by a government and used within a specific country.

current-density.desc: Current density is the amount of electric current flowing through a unit area, typically measured in amperes per square meter (A/m^2).

dynamic-fluid-viscosity.desc: Dynamic fluid viscosity is a measure of a fluid's resistance to flow under dynamic conditions, such as when it is being pumped or stirred.

electric-charge.desc: Electric charge is a fundamental property of matter, representing the amount of electricity in an object. It can be positive or negative.

electric-charge-density.desc: Electric charge density is the measure of electric charge per unit volume or area. It is denoted by the symbol ρ and is measured in coulombs per cubic meter or coulombs per square meter.

electric-current.desc: Electric current is the flow of electric charge through a conductor, measured in amperes (A). It is essential for powering electrical devices.

electric-dipole-moment.desc: Electric dipole moment is a measure of the separation of positive and negative charges in a system, representing a vector quantity.

electric-displacement-field.desc: Electric displacement field represents the electric flux density in a material medium, accounting for free and bound charge distributions.

electric-field-strength.desc: Electric field strength is a measure of the force exerted on a charged particle within an electric field.

electric-potential.desc: Electric potential is the amount of work needed to move a unit positive charge from a reference point to a specific point in an electric field.

electrical-conductance.desc: Electrical conductance is a measure of a material's ability to conduct electric current, typically measured in siemens (S).

electrical-conductivity.desc: "Electrical conductivity is a measure of a material's ability to conduct electric current."

electrical-resistivity.desc: Electrical resistivity is a measure of a material's ability to resist the flow of electric current.

energy.desc: Energy is the capacity to do work; Work is the transfer of energy; Torque is a measure of rotational force; Heat is a form of energy transfer; Spectral flux is the amount of radiant energy emitted per unit time.

entropy.desc: Entropy is a measure of disorder or randomness in a system, while heat capacity is the amount of heat energy required to change the temperature of a substance.

force.desc: Force is a physical quantity that measures the interaction between objects, while weight is the force of gravity acting on an object's mass.

frequency.desc: Frequency, Heart Rate measures how many times the heart beats per minute, indicating overall cardiovascular health and fitness level.

fuel-economy.desc: Fuel economy measures how efficiently a vehicle uses fuel to travel a certain distance, typically expressed in miles per gallon (mpg) or liters per 100 km.

gravitational-parameter.desc: Gravitational parameter is the product of the gravitational constant and the mass of a celestial body, often used in orbital mechanics calculations.

illuminance.desc: Illuminance is the measure of the amount of light falling on a surface, expressed in lux (lx).

impedance.desc: Impedance is the opposition to the flow of electrical current in a circuit, similar to electrical resistance.

inductance.desc: Inductance is the property of an electrical conductor that opposes changes in current flow, measured in henries.

irradiance.desc: Irradiance is the power of electromagnetic radiation per unit area, heat flux density is the rate of heat transfer per unit area, and radiosity is the total power radiated by a surface per unit area.

jerk.desc: Jerk is the rate of change of acceleration with respect to time, indicating how quickly an object's acceleration is changing.

jounce.desc: Jounce (jerk) is the rate of change of acceleration, while snap (jounce) is the rate of change of jounce.

length.desc: Length is a measurement of distance between two points, while wavelength is the distance between corresponding points on a wave.

linear-density.desc: Linear density is the measure of mass per unit length of a one-dimensional object such as a wire or string.

luminance.desc: Luminance is the measure of brightness of a light source or surface, perceived by the human eye.

luminous-efficacy.desc: Luminous efficacy measures how efficiently a light source produces visible light, expressed in lumens per watt.

luminous-efficacy-sr.desc: Luminous efficacy (sr) measures how efficiently a light source produces visible light, measured in lumens per watt within a solid angle.

luminous-energy.desc: Luminous energy is the measure of the total quantity of visible light emitted by a source over time.

luminous-energy-density.desc: Luminous energy density is the amount of light energy per unit volume, measured in lumens per cubic meter.

luminous-exposure.desc: "Luminous exposure measures the total amount of light received by a surface over a period of time, expressed in lux seconds."

luminous-flux.desc: Luminous flux, also known as luminous power, measures the total amount of visible light emitted by a source in all directions.

luminous-intensity.desc: Luminous intensity is the measure of the amount of light emitted in a specific direction, measured in candelas.

magnetic-field-strength.desc: Magnetic field strength is the measure of the magnetic field's intensity at a specific point, while magnetization is the magnetic moment per unit volume.

magnetic-flux.desc: Magnetic flux is a measure of the total magnetic field passing through a given surface, expressed in Weber (Wb).

magnetic-flux-density.desc: Magnetic flux density is a measure of the strength of a magnetic field within a given area.

magnetic-moment.desc: Magnetic moment is a measure of the strength and orientation of a magnet's magnetic field. It is represented by a vector.

mass.desc: Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object. It is a fundamental property that determines an object's inertia and gravitational attraction.

mass-density.desc: Mass density is the amount of mass per unit volume of a substance. Volume density is the amount of volume per unit volume. Concentration is the amount of a substance per unit volume of a mixture.

mass-flow-rate.desc: Mass flow rate is the amount of mass moving through a system per unit of time, while spectral exposure (fr) measures the amount of radiant energy at a specific frequency.

molar-concentration.desc: Molar concentration is a measure of the concentration of a solute in a solution, expressed in moles of solute per liter of solution.

molar-mass.desc: Molar mass is the mass of a substance divided by its amount in moles, expressed in grams per mole. It is a key concept in chemistry.

molar-volume.desc: Molar volume is the volume occupied by one mole of a substance at a specific temperature and pressure.

moment-of-inertia.desc: Moment of inertia is a measure of an object's resistance to changes in its rotational motion.

momentum.desc: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity; impulse is the change in momentum due to a force applied over a period of time.

optical-power.desc: Optical power measures the rate at which light energy is emitted or received. Wavenumber and wavevector describe the spatial frequency of waves.

permeability.desc: Permeability is a measure of a material's ability to allow fluids or gases to pass through it.

permittivity.desc: Permittivity is a measure of a material's ability to store electrical energy in an electric field.

plane-angle.desc: Plane angle measures rotation between two intersecting lines, often in degrees or radians.

pop.desc: "Pop is a unit of measurement used to quantify the amount of sound pressure in a given space, commonly used in the field of acoustics."

power.desc: Power, radiant flux, is the rate at which radiant energy is emitted, transmitted, or received per unit time.

pressure-gradient.desc: Pressure gradient is the rate of change of pressure over a distance in a fluid or gas, influencing the flow of fluids in various systems.

pressure.desc: Pressure is the force per unit area. Stress is the force applied to a material. Energy density is the amount of energy stored in a material. Spectral exposure (ln) measures the intensity of light at different wavelengths.

radiance.desc: Radiance is the amount of light energy emitted or reflected from a surface in a particular direction, measured in watts per square meter per steradian.

radiant-intensity.desc: Radiant intensity measures the power radiated by a source in a specific direction, typically expressed in watts per steradian.

reluctance.desc: Reluctance is the opposition to magnetic flux in a material, while electrical conductance is the ease with which electricity flows through a material.

solid-angle.desc: Solid angle is a measure of the extent of a cone-shaped region in space, representing the amount of 3D space an object subtends.

specific-energy.desc: Specific energy, Radioactive Dose is the amount of radiation absorbed by an object, measured in joules per kilogram or sieverts.

specific-heat-capacity.desc: Specific heat capacity is the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of a substance by one degree Celsius.

specific-intensity-fr.desc: Specific intensity (fr) is the amount of power per unit area, per unit solid angle, and per unit frequency, measured in watts per square meter per steradian per hertz.

specific-intensity-ln.desc: Specific intensity (ln) is the measure of radiant intensity per unit solid angle in a specific direction.

specific-volume.desc: Specific volume is the volume occupied by a unit mass of a substance, indicating how much space it occupies.

spectral-flux-ln.desc: Spectral flux (ln) measures the rate of change of a signal's spectral content, represented in logarithmic scale.

spectral-intensity-fr.desc: Spectral intensity (fr) refers to the amount of energy per unit frequency in a specific wavelength range.

spectral-intensity-ln.desc: Spectral intensity (ln) is a measure of the power per unit frequency bandwidth, expressed in natural logarithm scale.

spectral-irradiance-ln.desc: Spectral irradiance (ln) measures radiant flux per unit wavelength interval. It describes the amount of radiant energy emitted or received at different wavelengths.

surface-tension.desc: Surface tension is the force acting on the surface of a liquid, while spectral irradiance (fr) is the amount of radiant flux per unit area.

temperature.desc: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of particles in a substance, determining its hotness or coldness.

temperature-gradient.desc: Temperature gradient is the rate of change of temperature over a distance, indicating how quickly temperature changes in a given direction.

thermal-conductance.desc: Thermal conductance measures the ability of a material to conduct heat, expressed in watts per kelvin.

thermal-conductivity.desc: "Thermal conductivity measures a material's ability to conduct heat, determining how quickly heat energy can transfer through it."

thermal-resistance.desc: Thermal resistance measures a material's ability to resist heat flow, expressed in units of degrees Celsius per watt.

thermal-resistance-coefficient.desc: Thermal resistance coefficient measures the ability of a material to resist heat flow, expressed in units of degrees Celsius per watt (°C/W).

thermal-resistivity.desc: Thermal resistivity measures a material's resistance to heat flow. It is the reciprocal of thermal conductivity.

time.desc: Time is a fundamental physical quantity measuring the duration of events. Half-life is the time taken for a substance to decay by half. Labour refers to the physical and mental effort exerted in the production of goods and services.

unitless.desc: "Unitless" is a physical quantity that does not have any specific unit of measurement, typically used for ratios, angles, and pure numbers.

velocity.desc: Velocity is a measurement of the speed and direction of an object's motion. It is a vector quantity with units of meters per second (m/s).

viscosity.desc: Viscosity is a measure of a fluid's resistance to flow, influenced by its internal friction and cohesion.

volume.desc: Volume is the amount of space occupied by an object or substance, measured in cubic units.

volume-flow-rate.desc: Volume flow rate is the amount of fluid that passes through a given cross-sectional area per unit of time.
